subject: Creativity
title: Counterfactual Thinking: Imagining What Didn't Happen
description: A fast breakdown of Counterfactual Thinking: Imagining What Didn't Happen for builders.

hook.text: 'If I had left five minutes earlier...' That's counterfactual thinking — imagining alternative versions of past events.

buildup.text: Humans spontaneously generate counterfactuals after negative events. It's automatic — and evolutionarily useful.

discovery.text: Counterfactual thinking is how we learn from mistakes without repeating them.

twist.text: Silver medalists imagine the gold they missed; bronze medalists imagine missing the podium entirely.

climax.text: Entrepreneurs score higher on counterfactual thinking — they constantly imagine 'what if' scenarios that others don't.

punchline.text: Imagining what didn't happen teaches you more than remembering what did.

quiz.question: Why are Olympic silver medalists often less happy than bronze medalists?
options: They counterfactually think about almost winning gold
